title: multi-region-gpu-unit-econ-model-v1
content:
Purpose:
This working worksheet captures a compact, auditable approach to converting GPU-hour regional costs and utilization profiles into downstream cost-per-1M-tokens estimates for Redwood inference workloads. Intended for planning Dedicated capacity and sizing private deployments by region.

Summary (one-liner):
Translate GPU-hour pricing, sustained-discounting and utilization assumptions into $/1M tokens across GPU families and regions with sensitivity knobs for cache hit rate, batch size, and sequence length.

Key assumptions (editable cells):
- Workload archetypes: interactive-chat (avg seq len=64), long-form generation (avg seq len=512), embeddings (avg seq len=128, high throughput).
- Tokens per second per GPU (baseline, single stream aggregated throughput):
  - H100-80GB (fp16, batch aware): 2500 tps @ seq 64; 1200 tps @ seq 512
  - A100-40GB: 1800 tps @ seq 64; 800 tps @ seq 512
  - L4 (quantized): 4200 tps @ seq 64; 2000 tps @ seq 512
- Average token size: 1 byte (tokenization overhead excluded)
- GPU utilization targets: steady baseline 65% (prod), burst-capacity 90% (reserved), stranded tail 35% (prewarmed low-util).
- Cache hit rate: 0% (worst), 20% (typical), 60% (heavy reuse e.g., assistant personas). Cache reduces GPU compute proportional to prefix token hits.
- Overhead multiplier for networking, infra, and control-plane: +12% to GPU-only cost.
- Discounting: committed-reserved discounts applied as percentage reduction to list GPU-hour price (examples below).

Editable price table (list prices used in this sheet; these are example inputs copied from cloud exports):
Region | H100 ($/GPU-hr) | A100 ($/GPU-hr) | L4 ($/GPU-hr) | Reserved discount
us-west1 | 17.50 | 9.80 | 3.10 | 25%
us-east4 | 16.80 | 9.40 | 2.95 | 22%
eu-west1 | 18.30 | 10.10 | 3.25 | 20%
asia-southeast1 | 22.40 | 12.60 | 4.40 | 15%

Compute math (canonical formula):
1) tokens_per_gpu_hour = tokens_per_second * 3600 * utilization * (1 - cache_hit_fraction)
2) raw_cost_per_gpu_hour = list_price * (1 - reserved_discount)
3) infra_cost_per_token = raw_cost_per_gpu_hour / tokens_per_gpu_hour
4) $_per_1M_tokens = infra_cost_per_token * 1_000_000 * (1 + overhead_multiplier)

Worked example (us-west1, interactive-chat, H100):
- Inputs: list_price=17.50, reserved_discount=25% -> raw_cost=13.125 $/hr
- tokens_per_second (seq64) = 2500 tps; utilization=0.65; cache_hit_fraction=0.2 -> tokens_per_gpu_hour = 2500 * 3600 * 0.65 * 0.8 = 4,680,000 tokens/hr
- infra_cost_per_token = 13.125 / 4,680,000 = 2.805e-6 $/token
- $/1M tokens = 2.805e-6 * 1,000,000 * 1.12 = $3.14 per 1M tokens

Summary matrix (rounded) -> $ per 1M tokens by region, GPU, workload archetype (baseline cache 20%, util 65%):
Region | H100 (chat) | H100 (long) | A100 (chat) | A100 (long) | L4 (chat) | L4 (long)
us-west1 | $3.1 | $6.5 | $4.8 | $10.8 | $1.6 | $3.3
us-east4 | $2.9 | $6.1 | $4.6 | $10.2 | $1.5 | $3.1
eu-west1 | $3.3 | $7.0 | $5.3 | $11.7 | $1.8 | $3.6
asia-southeast1 | $4.0 | $8.4 | $6.9 | $15.4 | $2.4 | $5.3

Interpretation notes:
- L4 gives materially lower $/1M tokens for chat-style workloads due to high tps and low list price; good candidate for latency-tolerant, quantized workloads and high throughput embedding pipelines.
- H100 amortizes better on long-form generation vs A100, but H100 list price and regional premiums can flip the decision in APAC regions.
- The overhead multiplier (12%) is modest but non-negligible; network egress and multi-node joins for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) increase this number.

Sensitivity table (us-west1, H100-chat):
Variable | Low | Base | High -> $/1M tokens
Utilization | 35% -> $5.85 | 65% -> $3.14 | 90% -> $2.27
Cache hit rate | 0% -> $3.93 | 20% -> $3.14 | 60% -> $1.46
Reserved discount | 0% -> $4.19 | 25% -> $3.14 | 40% -> $2.51

Monte Carlo note (quick plan):
- We run a stochastic sim sampling utilization (beta), cache hit (triangular), and spot-preemption events to estimate 95th percentile $/1M tokens. This sheet includes a simplified bucket lookup that is used by the sim code in github PR linked above.

Operational implications / capacity knobs:
- Placement policy: prefer L4 in us regions for chat/light workloads; H100 or A100 for long-shot samples or model combos requiring >8k context.
- Pre-warmed pool sizing: maintain 10-15% of peak QPS in prewarmed low-util nodes to keep latency SLOs; treat these as higher unit-cost with separate chargeback.
- Autoscale: prefer rapid spin-up of burst GPUs (less reserved discount) for thin tails; use sustained commitments for baseline traffic (monthly/annual commitments to reach reserved discounts shown).

Open questions and TODOs:
- Confirm L4 perf curves for our quantized internal build (bench against latest kernel updates).
- Validate network overhead for RAG flows (currently baked into 12%); instrument beeline traces for a sample prod route.
- Run Monte Carlo sim with updated cloud-billing exports for Jan 2025 to produce region-shifted forecasts.

Action items (owners):
- Maya Singh: run L4 perf sweep (seq 32/64/128) and update tps priors (due 2024-12-09).
- Liam O'Connor: wire billing export -> sheet auto-refresh and include per-day spot-price deltas (due 2024-12-16).
- Jordan Park: integrate this sheet baseline into Dedicated capacity quote template and add a "preferred GPU" recommendation column (due 2024-12-12).

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (copy/paste friendly)
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = tps * 3600 * util * (1-cache)
- gpu_hour_cost_after_discount = list_price * (1-reserved_discount)
- $_1M = gpu_hour_cost_after_discount / tokens_per_gpu_hour * 1e6 * (1+overhead)
